entries.title: Audience-specific opening title
entries.observed_visual: Close presenter, then a listener reaction shot. The same three-line opening remains in a black rectangle below the face; ordinary captions replace it.
entries.observed_typography: White medium/bold sans-serif, sentence case, centered lines; opaque rectangular black backing, generous separation from the eyes. Exact family unknown.
entries.observed_timing: Static opening. The complete title clears at 3.837s in this source, on the return to the presenter.
entries.story_job: Identify the viewer this lesson serves before the explanation begins.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The opening addresses a new content creator; the following explanation contrasts depth with reach.
preserve: Three compact centered lines on one opaque backing; face stays clear.
Title is legible immediately and remains unchanged across the brief reaction cut.
Ordinary captions take over when the opening title leaves.
avoid: Do not animate an unrelated topic label and call it a hook.
Do not leave the opening title underneath later captions.
entries.use_when: A specific viewer situation makes the upcoming advice personally relevant.
entries.do_not_use_when: Understanding the hook requires seeing a product action or result.
entries.proposed_layout: Presenter full frame; title in safe lower-middle space; later captions use a separate clear reading zone.
entries.proposed_pacing: Set entrance, reading hold and removal from the new retained speech; reference duration is an observation, not a preset.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: Keep the person when expression or explanation is the evidence; return after an insert has done its specific job.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use the retained owned presenter footage and new source-supported copy; acquire any real supporting image before this scene is assembled.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Do not leave the opening title underneath later captions.
entries.implementation_adaptation: titlecard-calm is a candidate text host, not a static backed-title preset. Its exposed inputs are headline and kicker. Immediate visibility, removing drift/kicker gap, centered line layout and compact black backing require a bounded source/style adaptation. Prefer a verified native static-text host if one already supplies these properties. Set removal from the new speech.

preserve: Two readable lines with close-fitting colored backing above the face.
Headline remains stable while the underlying camera framing changes.
Headline clears when the qualification begins.
avoid: Do not repeat a long YouTube title over the person.
Do not apply the source's 8.467s lifetime to every new hook.

entries.do_not_use_when: The source only names the topic or never delivers an answer.

preserve: Large bold uppercase phrase develops in meaningful word groups.
A single contrasting emphasis phrase; presenter remains visible.
The full opening treatment disappears at the first explanatory close shot.
avoid: No old bullet-list graphics.
Do not omit the exception that makes the opening truthful.

There is no split=line API; line grouping belongs to the host layout.

entries.observed_timing: Header is present for the whole 21.2s source. Numeral changes at 12.350s; next shot starts at 12.383s.

preserve: One high-contrast top heading with a smaller context line.
Separate small section numeral beside the ordinary captions.
Header remains stable through shot changes; numeral changes with the lesson part.
avoid: Do not treat a persistent header as permission for three competing text layers.
Do not claim the website action is demonstrated; the reference only explains it.

entries.do_not_use_when: The title has become redundant or blocks the example needed next.

entries.proposed_pacing: Set entrance, reading hold and removal from the new retained speech; reference duration is an observation, not a preset.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: Keep the person when expression or explanation is the evidence; return after an insert has done its specific job.

Its two text roles need hierarchy/position changes; no exposed controls disable the entrance or drift. The persistent green heading, white context line and separate native section numeral need bounded layout/style adaptation. Never use a counter for the section marker.

entries.title: Plain captions over authentic performance
entries.observed_visual: A walking presenter holds a small microphone; gestures, changing background and camera distance vary the view. Only one white caption phrase is added at a time.
entries.observed_typography: Moderate white sentence-case sans-serif with a restrained dark edge/shadow, centered around torso height; no colored word emphasis or title card in these samples. Exact family unknown.
entries.observed_timing: Same composition family across 40.2s; caption phrases change with the words. This is not a verified zero-cut take.
entries.story_job: Preserve a clear conversational argument, gestures and physical movement.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The argument develops from a business problem through a qualification to a practical order of actions.
preserve: Small white sentence-case phrase captions in one stable reading zone.
Face, gestures and surroundings remain unobstructed.
Variation already present in walking and camera movement is preserved.
avoid: No new card just because two seconds elapsed.
Do not manufacture a results chart for a hypothetical benefit.
entries.use_when: The person's performance carries the lesson and no unshown mechanism needs explanation.
entries.do_not_use_when: A described action is hard to understand without seeing the operation or result.
entries.proposed_layout: Full presenter; captions occupy clear torso space and stay away from hands when those gestures matter.
entries.proposed_pacing: Set entrance, reading hold and removal from the new retained speech; reference duration is an observation, not a preset.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: Keep the person when expression or explanation is the evidence; return after an insert has done its specific job.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use the retained owned presenter footage and new source-supported copy; acquire any real supporting image before this scene is assembled.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Do not manufacture a results chart for a hypothetical benefit.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Use the existing timed-caption layer with plain white styling and a restrained shadow. Do not install a more complex animated caption demo merely to satisfy catalog usage.

entries.title: Cumulative framework reveal
entries.observed_visual: A dark green full frame replaces the speaker. The small word above, large cream ratio and final lower-right supporting word make three distinct text roles. Terms accumulate before the return to head.
entries.observed_typography: Heavy sans-serif; dominant cream ratio, much smaller white supporting words, broad empty margins. Left-aligned ratio with lower-right final word. Exact family unknown.
entries.observed_timing: Full-screen card spans 14.223–16.683s. Terms accumulate in successive steps; the cut back to presenter is clean.
entries.story_job: Give a compact framework a memorable structure after the problem is established.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The spoken explanation names a three-part allocation framework.
preserve: The existing numbers stay while the next term is added.
Strong type hierarchy on an uncluttered full-screen background.
Return to the presenter when the framework's first part begins.
avoid: Do not use count-up; this is cumulative structure, not changing quantity.
Do not force this card into the opening when the story has not established its purpose.
entries.use_when: A short named framework helps organize the explanation.
entries.do_not_use_when: The words describe actual operations that need to be shown rather than named.
entries.proposed_layout: Full visual for the brief reveal; no presenter inset; coherent type and color return as labels later.
entries.proposed_pacing: Set entrance, reading hold and removal from the new retained speech; reference duration is an observation, not a preset.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: Keep the person when expression or explanation is the evidence; return after an insert has done its specific job.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use the retained owned presenter footage and new source-supported copy; acquire any real supporting image before this scene is assembled.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Do not force this card into the opening when the story has not established its purpose.
entries.implementation_adaptation: kinetic-center-build is only a partial mechanism match: it accumulates whitespace-separated words and re-centers them. Exposed inputs are text, font_size, entry_offset, color and font_weight; there is no cues input. The slash-separated ratio needs deliberate token grouping and bounded source timing/alignment changes. Supporting words need separate native text roles. Preview the small adaptation before using it; this is not an already configured ratio card.

entries.title: Quiet category label that stays useful
entries.observed_visual: Presenter continues through wider and closer seated shots. One small category label stays above his head while separate white phrase captions accompany the speech.
entries.observed_typography: Bold cream sans-serif on compact dark green rounded backing; a single line. White smaller caption text stays visually separate. Exact family unknown.
entries.observed_timing: Three category labels hold about 13–14s each in this source; the first runs 16.683–30.614s.
entries.story_job: Keep the current category available while the presenter explains its examples.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The first portion of the framework is being defined and illustrated verbally.
preserve: One short top label; ordinary captions continue in their own zone.
Same label holds across framing changes.
Label leaves when its explanatory role ends.
avoid: Do not use the label as a substitute for the explanation.
Do not clear it on a universal three-second timer.

entries.do_not_use_when: The next beat needs this screen space for evidence or the category is already obvious.

Only headline/kicker are exposed: compact backing, removing the kicker gap, immediate visibility and no drift require source/style changes. Set the section interval explicitly.

entries.title: Brief real evidence insert
entries.observed_visual: A real consultation photo overlays the walking presenter, growing from a medium rectangle to a large one. The caption continues in front; the photo clears at the next idea.
entries.observed_typography: No photo title or browser chrome. Existing white phrase captions with dark edge remain the only added text. Preserve that simplicity.

preserve: A relevant real asset appears on the experience claim.
It occupies enough space to recognize the scene.
The insert clears so the explanation returns to the speaker.
avoid: Do not borrow the creator's photo for our own claim.
A consultation photo does not prove the exact client count or business result.

entries.do_not_use_when: Only generic stock imagery is available or the image would imply unproven results.

entries.title: Stacked original and output
entries.source_title: This AI Cloned Me in 15 Seconds
entries.observed_visual: Two video regions stack nearly equally: original person above, alternate output below. Both show moving faces/gestures; the caption sits across their boundary.
entries.observed_typography: White phrase captions with occasional turquoise emphasis and dark edge; two media panes supply the information. A caption treatment is independent of the split mechanism.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Let the viewer compare an original person and a digital-twin output while the claim is made.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The visible captions link the alternate output to the claim that it is a digital twin and moves like the source person.
preserve: Two large readable media regions, each with a clear reason to be present.
Compare corresponding source/output material, not unrelated B-roll.
Keep identifying faces and meaningful gestures inside both crops.
avoid: Do not shrink the evidence merely to retain a presenter badge.
Do not add a decorative wipe when simultaneous comparison is the point.
entries.use_when: The viewer benefits from inspecting two corresponding states simultaneously.
entries.do_not_use_when: Either pane becomes unreadable, or only one pane provides information.
entries.proposed_layout: Head full for assertion; top evidence/bottom head where both can fit; full evidence when text or comparison needs most of the frame.
entries.proposed_pacing: Hold through the visible action plus a readable settled result; references include four-second comparisons and five-second conversations.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: On interpretation, qualification or next question, after the result has been read.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use the retained speaker footage and obtain the actual result screen/video before designing the split. Inspect face and hand bounds on source frames; author a tracked crop only where source movement requires it. Record evidence at enough resolution to read the target at final portrait size.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Face/head tracking is a separate asset-analysis/crop task; a zoom catalog item does not perform it. A screen skeleton is not a product demonstration.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Use a native two-region media host. The source-inspected before-after-wipe was considered but is a horizontal reveal, not this static vertical stack. Existing media/layout primitives supply the scene; explicit portrait crop and synchronized media clocks are required.

entries.title: A request becomes a visible map
entries.source_title: Claude Can Now Plan Your Whole Day by Location
entries.observed_visual: A typed request fills the view; presenter and a brief service identity follow; a map with individual place pins then fills the upper region above the speaker.
entries.observed_typography: Product UI keeps its own readable text; the map scene uses a compact bold white uppercase caption near the pane boundary. UI branding is reference content, not our palette.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Turn a place-finding request into locations the viewer can inspect.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The request asks for breakfast, work and sightseeing places; the map is introduced as actual places.
preserve: The same request and relevant destinations carry into the result.
Map detail gets enough room to identify its pins.
Return to the presenter for interpretation after the map is understood.
avoid: Do not change city or task between request and map.
Do not treat a generic map as proof of the narrated itinerary.
entries.use_when: Place, route or spatial arrangement is what the viewer needs to understand.
entries.do_not_use_when: The spoken passage contains no spatial decision.
entries.proposed_layout: Full input while it is read; full map during route formation; split only when route labels remain legible.
entries.proposed_pacing: Reference request holds about4.5seconds; retain enough result hold for route and stops to be inspected.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After route resolves, to explain how it changes the day or what the limitation is.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Open the available mapping/chat workflow, choose one public example trip, record prompt submission and returned route in the same session. Save a clean wide capture plus close crops of request, place list and route. Keep city/stop names consistent; log the result source.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Reference mixes locations across inserts. Reuse the visual mechanism, not that discontinuity; a generic map is capability illustration, not proof of the narrated itinerary.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse browser-device-stage for an actual captured map/request. Compose with the presenter only while labels remain readable. Use ui-focus-zoom solely to enlarge a supplied target; it does not create the route.

entries.title: Show the usable product result
entries.source_title: I Gave an AI Engineer Access to My Whole Business
entries.observed_visual: A request screen leads through contextual material to a full-frame waitlist page. The next sample dims most of the page and isolates its form. The caption mentions a pull request that this form view does not prove.
entries.observed_typography: Small product text is subordinate to the large page headline and form target. Captions vary in the reference; reuse a coherent new caption system instead of copying every font change.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Show the output of a waitlist-page request, then focus on its useful control.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The passage asks for a waitlist page and describes what the agent produced. The form is visible; a separate pull-request outcome is unshown here.
preserve: The actual resulting interface fills enough of the frame to inspect.
Keep the same task identity from request to result.
Hold the resulting state after any action.
avoid: No decorative browser skeleton in place of the supplied result.
A visible form is not evidence of successful submission.
entries.use_when: The lesson promises a concrete output or working product.
entries.do_not_use_when: Only a hypothetical mockup exists but the words claim a completed real result.
entries.proposed_layout: Full input/constraints; split for site introduction; full form close-up for the operation.
entries.proposed_pacing: Reference prompt is about2.4seconds; form result needs at least a settled reading window after the action.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After the tested result, for the limitation or how the viewer can reproduce it.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use an owned test project. Obtain the actual generated page, record navigating to the form, entering permitted sample data, clicking and showing the response. Keep any live external submission inside an authorized demo environment.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: A highlighted input is not evidence of a pull request or successful submission. Capture those outcomes separately if claimed.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse ui-focus-zoom on a real capture. Use a simple media host without adding nested browser chrome. Capture any claimed interaction/confirmation and align its action cue.

entries.title: One supported number becomes prominent
entries.source_title: Claude Can Now Plan Your Whole Day by Location
entries.observed_visual: A service identity sits above a large 50,000 value; a smaller free-transactions line appears underneath. This upper graphic stays above the presenter. The digits develop before the context line completes.
entries.observed_typography: Bold white value, smaller white unit/context line, green gridded upper field. The source describes an allowance, not an achieved client count or adoption metric.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Make the size of a stated free allowance easy to understand.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The passage describes 50,000 free transactions. Preserve the unit and verify the applicable terms for any new claim.
preserve: One dominant value with its unit and necessary qualification.
Keep supporting words much smaller than the value.
Use the same type/color system as the rest of the short.
avoid: Do not invent a result or confuse a goal with an achieved metric.
Do not add a chart when the point is one number.
entries.use_when: A sourced quantity itself is the payoff or useful comparison anchor.
entries.do_not_use_when: Several variables need a relationship that one large number cannot explain.
entries.proposed_layout: Full number or simple upper stage; no competing paragraph; head interprets the significance.
entries.proposed_pacing: Roughly1–3seconds after entrance for a simple number; longer if it needs qualification.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: When turning magnitude into a useful implication or next step.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Obtain the actual allowance, unit, current applicable terms and source date for the product being explained. Preserve any necessary account/tier qualification. Use a clearly labelled illustrative quantity only if the speech is hypothetical.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: The reference displays a free-transactions allowance. Re-check current eligibility and terms before using a similar claim; do not change it into a claim of achieved results.
entries.implementation_adaptation: number-pop-in is an inspected markup/style snippet with a commented GSAP integration recipe, not a self-running finished component. Wire its digit animation into the parent timeline and use a separate native text role for the lower context line (its suffix is inline). Keep the value supported; use a bounded staged reveal, not an invented intermediate count-up.

entries.title: Let the viewer follow the input
entries.source_title: I Build Features Just By Talking to My Code
entries.observed_visual: Presenter with a keyboard cue gives way to a centered listening window. Requirements accumulate inside it with a separate key graphic below; a progress/task view follows.
entries.observed_typography: Small monospace-like application text inside a light window, large bold key label below, neutral background. Capture legibility matters more than adding typography.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Make voice activation and the developing instruction visible.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The speaker names the key and then describes the requirements and work the system can perform.
preserve: The input visibly develops rather than being replaced by a noun label.
The specific request matches the eventual result.
Keep the listening/key cue distinct from the content being entered.
avoid: Do not replace a voice-input state with a mouse-click ripple.
Do not cut away before the viewer can understand the request.
entries.use_when: How a command enters the system is part of the lesson.
entries.do_not_use_when: The input is obvious and only the output needs attention.
entries.proposed_layout: Head for instruction, full composer for readable requirements, split for clarification, full dashboard for payoff.
entries.proposed_pacing: Reference’s typing action lasts about6.65seconds; preserve that kind of reading window when the requirement matters.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After using one visible dashboard control, to explain what the approval changed.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Use owned demo data and a support-dashboard request. Record input activation, final transcribed instruction, one consequential follow-up, approval and operating result. Save native screen capture; retain source/result identity.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Reference uses a Mars signup output following support-dashboard requirements. That is capability montage, not same-run completion evidence.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse browser-device-stage with chrome=window and a capture of the actual listening/input behavior. If no capture exists, an illustrative key/listening state must be authored explicitly; the item does not supply it.

entries.title: A shared hub connects multiple clients
entries.source_title: Give ChatGPT and Claude the Same Memory
entries.observed_visual: A central two-line memory identity has eight glowing spokes ending in separate client icons and labels. The complete diagram fills the frame with no presenter.
entries.observed_typography: Bright white and purple central text; small white labels under recognizable icons, blue/purple connectors on black. Exact brand marks are content dependencies, not built-in catalog nodes.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Explain that several clients can connect to one shared memory.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The surrounding passage generalizes the shared-memory behavior across multiple models/tools.
preserve: One central object and several actual connections.
Preserve the hub-and-spoke topology.
Reveal or emphasize the relevant path, then allow the complete map to be read.
avoid: Do not turn this into a linear sequence or generic list.
Do not use logos for integrations the new script does not support.
entries.use_when: Several things share one central resource or capability.
entries.do_not_use_when: The real logic is a chain, hierarchy or feedback loop.
entries.proposed_layout: Full diagram for the generalization; no presenter needed while eight labels compete for space.
entries.proposed_pacing: Reference holds this about3.67seconds; use at least a readable settled state after paths appear.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: On control, limitation or what the viewer should connect first.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Obtain permitted brand assets or use legible text labels. Define the actual supported clients and whether the connection is one-way/two-way before drawing arrows; keep one shared object identity from the preceding demo.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Do not replace a chain, tree or worker grid with this hub simply because both have nodes. Directionality and topology must match the lesson.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse constellation-hub for the actual hub topology. hub_label, nodes, cues and exit are real inputs. Nodes render text labels; there is no icon/image node input. Prefer readable text labels, or compose required permitted icons explicitly. Size the host for portrait, align cues and hold the complete map; exit=none allows the host to cut cleanly.

entries.title: Delegation branches and returns
entries.source_title: Huge ChatGPT Update You Need to See!
entries.observed_visual: An upper panel contains a chief, three task branches, three outputs and a return connector. The speaker remains below. The diagram is already largely complete in these samples and gently changes scale.
entries.observed_typography: Compact white labels, red chief node, orange task nodes, circular outputs, thin directional connectors on a dark panel. Small connector labels are hard to read at phone size.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Give a named chief-of-staff system a visible organization.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The sampled captions introduce the speaker's own AI chief of staff; the diagram supplies role, output and return structure beyond the short spoken label.
preserve: Distinct outgoing branches, each connected to its own output.
Visible return/aggregation path to the original chief.
Stable overview after the relationship has been revealed.
avoid: Do not call a hub or a simple list an equivalent.
Do not show a feedback arrow unless the described process has that feedback.
entries.use_when: The lesson requires delegation, separate outputs and aggregation or feedback.
entries.do_not_use_when: There is only a central hub without a directional work/return sequence.
entries.proposed_layout: Full visual if branch labels need room; split only with short labels and sufficient top-stage height.
entries.proposed_pacing: A two-second reference glimpse establishes a category but cannot teach a complex loop; plan3–6seconds or simplify to one branch before expanding.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After outputs converge, to say what decision the chief enables.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Write the three assignments and concrete outputs from the lesson. Create only those nodes. If claiming live delegation, capture real role runs and attach their actual results instead of fake completion badges.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Color changes cannot repair wrong relationship anatomy. A simple hub lacks distinct stage/feedback meaning.
entries.implementation_adaptation: No inspected item implements the complete branch-and-return scene unchanged. Build only this missing topology using the inspected flowchart-vertical/whiteboard-ink connector mechanisms and a native host. The layout and cue order need a small preview before reuse; this is a documented gap, not a ready-made template.

entries.title: Give story footage the full frame
entries.source_title: OpenArt Director: The New Way to Make AI Videos
entries.observed_visual: A prompt gives way to several full visual examples. Landscape shots use blurred duplicate fill above/below; a later portrait shot fills the frame. The examples change story/character, so this is a montage of capabilities.
entries.observed_typography: Small white/turquoise captions over actual result footage. Most of the frame is reserved for the moving scene; no presenter inset or decorative container.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Give the moving output enough space for the viewer to inspect its appearance.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The words describe direction and consistency while the source shows multiple cinematic examples. The montage does not establish same-story continuity.
preserve: Use full-frame footage when the imagery is the information.
Keep subject/project continuity across the selected shots.
Return to the presenter when interpretation adds value.
avoid: Do not overlay an unrelated card over the result.
Do not use this as proof of character consistency unless the actual sequence supports that claim.
entries.use_when: The viewer needs to see a moving result, event or story moment.
entries.do_not_use_when: The only available asset is unrelated stock footage.
entries.proposed_layout: Full prompt for initial instruction; split planning views; full output sequence; split timeline for interpretation.
entries.proposed_pacing: Give the connected output sequence several seconds so consistency is visible; do not reduce it to isolated still flashes.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After the timeline/output sequence, to explain why directing beats assembling unrelated clips.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Choose one small owned story. Obtain brief, storyboard, character sheet,3–4related output shots and editor timeline. Record selecting one scene and inspecting the corresponding output; avoid swapping to an unrelated example at payoff.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Reference jumps among earthquake, Mighty Mishap, red-haired character and boat/monster examples. Study their presentation mechanics while keeping our proof within one story.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Use actual source/result video in the native media lane. screen-flow-carousel was considered but is unnecessary furniture for full-frame playing footage. Obtain the required moving assets during planning; HyperFrames composes them but does not generate the acted scene.

entries.title: Readable artifact above the speaker
entries.source_title: ClickUp Brain2: The AI That Replaces All Your Software
entries.observed_visual: Conversation above presenter, then full presenter, then another request, then a readable slide above presenter. The displayed sample request and slide concern different projects.
entries.observed_typography: The slide has a dominant black/orange headline on white; small source UI remains peripheral. Caption sits near the pane boundary. Dense body copy would need a larger crop.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Show what the generated presentation looks like while the speaker explains it.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The passage moves from conversation and sample prompt to opening the slide. A new edit should keep the actual request and output from the same project.
preserve: The artifact's important content stays legible at phone size.
Presenter remains useful for interpretation.
Enlarge to full artifact when detail no longer fits the split.
avoid: No tiny full-browser screen with unreadable text.
Do not keep the presenter merely as a compulsory identity badge.
entries.use_when: A diagram, slide or document benefits from simultaneous explanation.
entries.do_not_use_when: The artifact needs the entire portrait frame to be read.
entries.proposed_layout: Full request when it requires reading; split deck with presenter for live explanation; full deck if body text is important.
entries.proposed_pacing: Reference sample prompt8seconds and conversation5.5seconds show legitimate sustained actions. Hold each useful slide until the highlighted claim is readable, not for every paragraph.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: After demonstrating the artifact, to discuss input quality or the practical next step.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Obtain permitted source facts, run one request and retain the produced deck. Record its opening and navigation in the same project. If using mock data, keep the sample label visible and do not imply investor metrics are real.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Reference Glaido example prompt differs from the shown monthly-business deck; use the real matched output. modal-morph is experimental and needs deterministic seek/reload validation before production.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse ui-focus-zoom inside a native stacked presenter/artifact host. Supply the actual slide/capture and target coordinates; move to full evidence for dense detail. This reuses the same host family as P01 with different content roles.

entries.title: Change one option inside a stable phrase
entries.source_title: ClickUp Brain2: The AI That Replaces All Your Software
entries.observed_visual: A fixed phrase remains while model names move through a vertical slot, leaving fainter neighboring options above. The colored upper stage sits above the speaker, then clears back to full presenter.
entries.observed_typography: Light sans-serif option names with small icons on a dark purple field; one active row is bright, prior rows fade. Caption below is separate bold white/turquoise.
entries.observed_timing: The sequence shows selected source states; inspect the original interval for exact motion, easing and spoken synchronization.
entries.story_job: Make the breadth of choices in one category visually concrete.
entries.spoken_or_caption_cue_paraphrase: The speaker refers to different chat models; the fixed phrase and changing option slot reinforce that category.
preserve: Stable grammatical frame and one changing choice.
Only the option slot changes; surrounding meaning stays clear.
Leave each necessary option readable.
avoid: Do not rotate unrelated slogans to simulate variety.
Do not show outdated or unavailable choices as current capabilities.
entries.use_when: The lesson is about several choices within one consistent category.
entries.do_not_use_when: The entire proposition or causal relationship changes.
entries.proposed_layout: Type above head for breadth; full or large crop of actual menu for selection.
entries.proposed_pacing: Names may cycle quickly, but hold the real menu long enough to find the option being recommended.
entries.proposed_return_to_head: At the recommendation of which option to choose and why.
entries.proposed_asset_brief: Inspect the available model menu in the actual target app. Save a legible capture and use only the options present for the account/workspace being explained.
entries.reference_limit_to_improve: Typographic brand names establish identity; they do not prove access, model quality or account eligibility.
entries.implementation_adaptation: Reuse kinetic-type-swap with fixed prefix/suffix, explicit options and cue times. Supply valid choices from the new source, then reveal the actual menu if availability is claimed.
